title: client snooze/resume handshake with quarantined toolcall semantics (OpenAI-compat)
author: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: Introduces a client "snooze"/resume handshake extension to the streaming protocol plus a quarantined tool-call window to ensure idempotent tool invocation at reconnect.
Motivation: in production we observed customer load patterns where transient client suspensions (mobile backgrounding, flaky NATs) caused either premature server-side tool replays or long tail ticket incidents due to duplicated tool calls. This change reduces duplicate tool invocations while preserving fast resumability and OpenAI-compatible semantics.
Design notes: added a lightweight "snooze" state that clients can enter before disconnecting; server issues a short-lived Quarantine Token associated with in-flight toolcalls; when client reconnects it performs a ResumeHandshake that can claim, re-run or let expire quarantined toolcalls. The handshake is backward-compatible: if the adapter on the other side does not support the extension, fallback to previous lease/fencing behavior.
Checklist:
- [x] design doc: internal link to /docs/design/stream-snooze-resume (rev 3)
- [x] protocol extension draft on wire format and handshake codes
- [x] server implementation: snooze manager, quarantine token lifecycle, eviction policy
- [x] adapter change in openai-compat to surface new header for ResumeHandshake
- [x] integration tests for claim/expire/replay scenarios
- [x] perf smoke showing <1% median latency regression under 95th percentile load
Changes included:
- protocol: added ResumeHandshake V1b with optional header X-Resume-Token and Handshake-Ack codes
- server: new service packages/streaming-protocol/src/snooze_manager.rs responsible for issuing and reconciling quarantined toolcalls, TTLs, and small in-memory tombstones to avoid double-execution
- openai-compat adapter: read ResumeHandshake header and translate to adapter-specific toolcall idempotency metadata
- console: added stream-inspector tooling for visualizing quarantined toolcalls and client snooze state
- tests: new integration-suite with simulated client suspend/reconnect under different clock skews
Commits (high-level):
- a1f3b2f: add snooze manager module and basic lifecycle
- b2d4e8c: wire ResumeHandshake into transport layer and adapter shim
- c3e9f17: integrate quarantine token behavior into toolcall executor with expiration/claim paths
- d4f0a22: unit and integration tests covering claim, replay, and expire flows
- e5a1ff9: add console inspector and docs
Changeset (selected files):
- packages/streaming-protocol/src/snooze_manager.rs: new module ~180 lines implementing TTLs, claim/expire logic and metrics hooks
- packages/openai-adapter/src/handshake.rs: adapter handling for X-Resume-Token and compatibility fallback
- server/protocols/stream/README.md: protocol summary and compatibility table
- packages/console/src/stream-inspector.ts: UI helpers to show quarantined toolcalls
- docs/openai-compat/stream-snooze.md: public-facing compatibility notes and recommended client behavior
- integration-tests/streaming/snooze_resume.test.ts: end-to-end scenarios with deterministic clocks
Review conversation (high-level):
- Liam O'Connor (reviewer): "Nice end-to-end. Two concerns: (1) eviction TTL default seemed optimistic; recommend 30s not 10s for mobile churn, (2) metrics: add a per-model duplicated-toolcall gauge so we can alert if quarantine fails".
- Maya (author): "Adjusted TTL to 30s in config and added duplicated-toolcall gauge exposed via metrics/snooze.*. Also added config knob for enterprise customers to lengthen TTL up to 5m.".
- Sofia Ramirez: "Please add a more explicit fallback test when the OpenAI adapter doesn't implement the header (we should assert behavior is unchanged).".
- Maya: "Added explicit adapter-fallback test and verified existing behavior (lease fencing) remains intact.".
- Evan Liu: "Request to add documentation on billing implications for claimed vs expired toolcalls (since some toolcalls incur external costs).".
- Maya: "Added a short section in docs/openai-compat/stream-snooze.md explaining billing semantics and recommended guardrails for expensive toolcalls.".
CI summary: Full CI passed after one flaky integration job rerun. Checks run: lint (pass), unit (pass), integration (flaky initially, rerun pass), e2e (pass), perf-smoke (pass within 2% of baseline).
Observability and metrics: added metrics/snooze.quarantined_count, metrics/snooze.claims, metrics/snooze.expirations, metrics/snooze.duplicate_toolcalls. Added tracing spans for ResumeHandshake and quarantine transitions.
Backwards compatibility: handshake is optional; adapter falls back to existing lease/fencing semantics if header absent.
Migration notes: no migration required for existing customers; feature gated behind runtime config flag streaming.snooze.enabled=false by default on older clusters; rollout plan: enable opt-in for early customers, monitor metrics for duplicates then flip on by cohort.
Performance: microbenchmarks show negligible CPU overhead and <1% median latency change at p95 under our perf-canary workload; batching unchanged.
Release notes: "Streaming: add client snooze/resume handshake and quarantined toolcall window to reduce duplicate tool invocations on reconnects; opt-in via runtime config; OpenAI-compat adapter updated to translate ResumeHandshake tokens. See docs/openai-compat/stream-snooze.md for details.".
Merge: squash-and-merge into main; commit message summarizes design, configuration flags, and keys to monitor.
Post-merge actions:
- publish docs/openai-compat/stream-snooze.md to docs site
- add alert rule if metrics/snooze.duplicate_toolcalls > 0.1% of calls over 5m
- schedule rollout to beta tenants and monitor for 48h
- follow up with SDK teams to expose recommended client snooze examples in mobile quickstarts
